subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should WhatsApp call activity be exposed only as an opt-in ephemeral plugin event, or should OpenClaw also retain and query it as contact history?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the missing listener, but code cannot determine the intended privacy, retention, identity, configuration, and public API contracts for a new category of personal activity metadata.

options.title: Ephemeral plugin event
options.body: Add an opt-in sanitized WhatsApp call event with access-control checks and no durable call-history storage by default.

options.title: Persist contact activity
options.body: Design a generic retained contact-activity model with explicit identity, retention, deletion, migration, and query contracts before wiring calls into it.

options.title: Do not expose calls
options.body: Keep call activity outside OpenClaw because the privacy and maintenance cost outweighs the reminder use case.

recommendation.title: Ephemeral plugin event
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in sanitized WhatsApp call event with access-control checks and no durable call-history storage by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The current WhatsApp event, configuration, and outbound-call history plus the issue-scoping comment make this the strongest available product-routing candidate.
